summary: The starter prompt gives a clear high-level goal (Python LangChain single-agent that scores ESG pillars, stores scores+rationales+embeddings, and runs an aggregation ranking). Many DocumentDB operational details (connection env var, cluster tier) are provided in the sample's run-environment note, and the installed DocumentDB skills cover index and client best practices. Missing specifics the builder will assume: exact Python/runtime and driver versions, which embedding & chat model/provider and their env var names, a concrete document schema and embedding field name, seed-data contents and size, and whether to expose a /search API vs CLI. These assumptions are routine, so the build can start but will fill gaps with defaults.

rubric.found_in_prompt: build a Python LangChain agent that reads company ESG data documents from DocumentDB, uses prompt engineering to instruct the LLM to score each pillar (E, S, G) on a 1-10 scale with reasoning, embeds the rationale for semantic search, and writes the scored document back. Add an aggregation pipeline that ranks companies by composite ESG score.
rubric.note: Clear high-level business problem and demo objective.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use Python 3.10 (or the venv's python), target a recent pip/pymongo-compatible runtime (3.10/3.11). Package / requirements will be made to work on Python 3.10+.
rubric.note: Prompt says Python but gives no version. The sample's run-environment note states 'python and pip resolve to a virtual environment', but not the interpreter version.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use pymongo (the official Python MongoDB driver), pinned to a recent 4.x release compatible with MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol (e.g., pymongo>=4.4,<5.0). Follow singleton MongoClient pattern.
rubric.note: The documentdb-driver skill provides the singleton-client / reuse guidance but does not assert an exact version; the builder will pick a recent pymongo 4.x release.

rubric.found_in_prompt: A vector-capable Azure DocumentDB cluster (compute tier M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol, DiskANN, HNSW and IVF vector indexes) is reachable from this machine. Its connection string is in the environment variable `DOCUMENTDB_URI`.
rubric.note: Run-environment (skill_md) explicitly gives the cluster tier and wire protocol.

rubric.found_in_prompt: The connection string is in the environment variable `DOCUMENTDB_URI`.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Database connection string read from env var DOCUMENTDB_URI; LLM/embedding API key(s) read from standard env vars like OPENAI_API_KEY (or provider-specific vars). The builder will not hard-code secrets and will include a .env.example.
rubric.note: DB credential location is specified in the run note; the prompt does not name any LLM/embedding env vars.

rubric.found_in_prompt: reads company ESG data documents from DocumentDB ... writes the scored document back
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Create a simple schema within collection `companies` (or `esg_companies`) with fields: `_id`, `name`, `raw_esg_text` (source text), numeric `score_E`, `score_S`, `score_G`, string `rationale_E`, `rationale_S`, `rationale_G`, `rationale_embedding` (array of floats), and `schemaVersion`.
rubric.note: The prompt names the domain but doesn't define field names or types; the data-modeling skill guides embedding vs referencing and schemaVersion best-practices.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Provide a small synthetic seed set (e.g., 8–12 company documents with `raw_esg_text`) loaded by a seed script. The seed script will be idempotent (upsert by company name or _id).
rubric.note: The starter prompt doesn't specify sample data source, size or license; local-deployment skill gives patterns but not actual sample data.

rubric.found_in_prompt: embeds the rationale for semantic search
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Create a cosmosSearch vector index (one of vector-hnsw, vector-ivf or vector-diskann) on `rationale_embedding`. Choose vector-hnsw or diskann based on dataset size (HNSW for <50k, diskann for larger). Dimensions will match embedding model output (assume 1536 unless model chosen differs).
rubric.note: The installed vector-search and indexing skills provide exact guidance and index-creation patterns; the prompt didn't name index-creation API or vector subtype explicitly, so the skill will guide the concrete choice.

rubric.found_in_prompt: uses prompt engineering to instruct the LLM to score each pillar ... embeds the rationale for semantic search
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use OpenAI as a default provider with an embedding model such as text-embedding-3-small (1536 dims) and an LLM (gpt-4o-mini or gpt-4o) via LangChain. API keys come from OPENAI_API_KEY. Normalize embeddings for cosine similarity.
rubric.note: Prompt requires LLM + embeddings but doesn't specify provider, models, or dims. These decisions materially affect index dims and code.

rubric.found_in_prompt: build a Python LangChain agent ... Add an aggregation pipeline that ranks companies by composite ESG score.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Deliver a command-line sample tool (CLI) with commands: `seed` (load data & create index), `process` (run agent to score & write documents), `aggregate` (run aggregation to rank companies), and `search` (small Flask/FastAPI endpoint or CLI subcommand to run semantic search).
rubric.note: Prompt does not mandate CLI vs API or routes like /search; reference requirements expect a /search route, but prompt doesn't require it.

rubric.found_in_prompt: This sample is being built on a developer machine where an Azure DocumentDB cluster is already provisioned and reachable. ... Do not provision another cluster unless the run policy says Azure writes are allowed; the cluster above is the one to use.
rubric.note: Run-environment explicitly says a cluster exists and should be used; builder will not create cloud infra.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Provide a README with commands: `pip install -r requirements.txt`, copy `.env.example` to `.env` and set vars, `python -m sample.seed` to seed, `python -m sample.process` to run the agent, `python -m sample.aggregate` to run ranking, and `pytest` for tests (unit tests will mock DB).
rubric.note: The starter prompt doesn't include explicit run/test commands; local-deployment skill gives guidance for local workflows.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Accept when: code scores every company doc with numeric E/S/G (1–10) and rationale strings, attachments store embedding arrays, a vector index is created and usable, the aggregation pipeline returns companies ranked by composite score, and a README explains setup and run.
rubric.note: No explicit acceptance criteria in the prompt.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Keep sample small and inexpensive (no provisioning of clusters), avoid production HA or CMK configuration; note in README that this is a demo, not production-ready.
rubric.note: No cost or compliance constraints given; data-modeling skill reminds of 16 MB limit etc.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use common gallery layout: README.md, requirements.txt (pinned), sample/ package with seed/process/aggregate modules, tests/ with mocks, .env.example, and scripts/ for seed. Use 'Azure DocumentDB' naming in README and code comments.
rubric.note: Prompt doesn't specify repository layout or README contents; local-deployment skill recommends versioned seed/index scripts and env-driven config.

questions_for_author: Which embedding provider and model should the sample use (e.g., OpenAI text-embedding-3-small with 1536 dims)? This determines index dimensions and env var names.
Which LLM/chat model (provider + model id) should the LangChain agent call for scoring, and what env var name(s) should hold its credentials?
Should the sample expose a web /search route (and return similarity scores) or just provide CLI commands? The reference requirements expect a /search route but the starter prompt doesn't name it.
Which Python and pymongo version should be targeted/pinned in requirements.txt (e.g., Python 3.10 and pymongo>=4.4,<5.0)?

Is creating the cosmosSearch vector index in code required for this run (the reference requires it) even though a live cluster already exists? The run-environment warned against provisioning new clusters; is index creation allowed on the existing cluster?
requirements_at_risk: Create a cosmosSearch vector index in Azure DocumentDB in code (using createSearchIndexes) on the stored embedding field — not explicitly requested in the starter prompt; the builder may or may not create the index unless prompted.

Store embeddings as an array of floats on the document (the embedding field) — the prompt says 'embeds the rationale' but does not explicitly state storage format; builder will assume array-of-floats but this is not specified.

The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables — DB conn string is specified (DOCUMENTDB_URI) in skill_md, but model/embedding credentials are not named and may be assumed (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY).
.env.example lists every setting with placeholder values — prompt doesn't request a .env.example; it's likely to be omitted unless the builder follows gallery conventions.

The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output — embedding model/dimensions are unspecified, so the index dimensions might be chosen incorrectly if the builder picks a different model.
The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one — prompt doesn't instruct to document or tune parameters for scale.
A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data — no sample-data source or idempotent seed script is specified.
/search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails — the prompt doesn't require a /search route or error behavior.
Search results include the similarity score — not specified; builder may or may not include similarity in results.
Dependencies are pinned in requirements.txt — prompt doesn't mention pinning versions; builder may or may not pin them.
Unit tests run without a live cluster — tests are not specified; without explicit guidance the builder may not provide mocked tests.

Infrastructure for the cluster provided as code using the Azure DocumentDB resource type — run-environment forbids provisioning a new cluster and prompt doesn't ask for infra-as-code, so infra code may be missing.
README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up — README content is not specified and may be incomplete.
